# awscontrib_connect_data_table_record (Resource)

Manages one non-default Amazon Connect data-table record. The values map is authoritative for every value in the remote record, and same-table mutations are serialized within one provider process.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "awscontrib_connect_data_table_record" "example" {
  instance_id   = "aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-111111111111"
  data_table_id = awscontrib_connect_data_table.example.id

  primary_values = {
    customer_id = "customer-123"
    channel     = "voice"
  }

  values = {
    routing_group = "priority"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `data_table_id` (String) Amazon Connect data-table identifier.
- `instance_id` (String) Amazon Connect instance identifier.
- `primary_values` (Map of String) Nonempty composite primary key, keyed by primary attribute name. Changing it replaces the record.
- `values` (Map of String) Nonempty authoritative set of record values keyed by non-primary attribute name. Remote values absent from configuration are deleted.

### Read-Only

- `record_id` (String) Amazon Connect record identifier derived from the composite primary key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import awscontrib_connect_data_table_record.example 'aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-111111111111:aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-555555555555:aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-666666666666'
```
